purpose: Calcitonin salmon is used to treat osteoporosis in women who are at least 5 years past menopause, helping to reduce the risk of spine fractures. It is also used to treat Paget's disease of bone and to lower dangerously high calcium levels in the blood. This medication helps keep your bones stronger and your calcium levels in a safe range.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a hormone called calcitonin that helps control how much calcium is in your blood and bones. This medication is a man-made version of that hormone, derived from salmon, which works very similarly in humans. It works by slowing down the cells that break down bone, which helps keep your bones denser and stronger and helps keep calcium levels balanced.
common_side_effects: Nasal spray form may cause a runny nose, nosebleeds, or nasal irritation. The injectable form can cause nausea, flushing of the face, or redness and irritation at the injection site. Some people may also experience mild dizziness or headache.
warnings: Long-term use has been linked to a slightly increased risk of certain cancers, so your doctor will regularly review whether you still need this medication. Tell your doctor if you are allergic to fish or salmon before starting this medication. It is not recommended for use during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Rarely, serious allergic reactions can occur, so seek medical help immediately if you have trouble breathing, swelling of the face, or a rash.
typical_dosing: For osteoporosis, the nasal spray dose is usually one spray (200 units) into one nostril every day, alternating nostrils each day. For injectable forms, dosing varies depending on the condition being treated and your doctor will guide you on how and where to inject it. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
